root_cause.text: The struct papr_hvpipe_hdr is stack-allocated and only partially initialized (hdr.version and hdr.flags), leaving reserved padding bytes uninitialized, which are then copied to userspace via copy_to_user(), causing a kernel stack memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states: "The hdr variable is allocated on the stack and only hdr.version and hdr.flags are initialized explicitly. Because the struct papr_hvpipe_hdr contains reserved padding bytes (reserved[3] and reserved2[40]), these could leak the uninitialized bytes to userspace after copy_to_user()." The patch changes the declaration to `hdr = {}` to zero-initialize the entire struct.

bic_trace_step.reason: In papr_hvpipe_handle_read(), struct papr_hvpipe_hdr hdr is stack-allocated and only hdr.version and hdr.flags are set to 0 (lines: 'hdr.version = 0; hdr.flags = 0;'). The entire hdr (HVPIPE_HDR_LEN bytes) is then copied to userspace via copy_to_user() (line: 'ret = copy_to_user(buf, &hdr, HVPIPE_HDR_LEN);'). This leaves any padding bytes in the struct uninitialized, causing a kernel stack memory leak. No memset or zero-initialization of the whole struct is present.
